identity.spiritualSignificanceShort: Naina Devi is revered as one of the Shakti Peethas, where tradition holds that the right eye ("naina") of Sati fell. The hilltop shrine above the town of the same name in Bilaspur district is a major pilgrimage site, especially during Navratri.

governance.establishedEra: Traditional account; exact founding century not documented in sources consulted

narrative.summaryIntro: Naina Devi Temple sits atop a hill above the town of Naina Devi in Bilaspur district, Himachal Pradesh. Regarded as one of the Shakti Peethas, it is reached by road partway up the hill and then by steps or cable car to the summit, and draws large crowds of pilgrims, particularly during Navratri.
narrative.documentedHistory: According to temple tradition, the site is one of the Shakti Peethas, marking the spot where Sati's right eye fell after Vishnu dismembered her body. A separate local legend holds that a Gujjar boy discovered the site after seeing a cow shower milk on a stone, and reported this in a dream to Raja Bir Chand, who then built a temple there. The temple gained wider public attention after a stampede during Navratri on 3 August 2008, in which a large number of pilgrims died.

festivals.significance: The temple's main pilgrimage season, drawing very large crowds; a stampede during Navratri on 3 August 2008 is a documented safety incident at the site.
